paper.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models

repo.description: Microsoft LoRA — low-rank adaptation of large language models.

annotation_metadata.review_scope: Repository revision, PyTorch import, and all annotated symbol locations checked against pinned source; existing claim text and labels preserved.
annotation_metadata.paper_evidence_note: Original PDF bytes have not been verified for this metadata review. Claim text is curated; existing section/page/character spans must not be treated as verified PDF quotations.

claims.text: LoRA injects trainable low-rank decomposition matrices A and B alongside each frozen pretrained weight matrix.
The forward pass computes h = W_0 x + (B A) x scaled by alpha / r.
Matrix A is initialized with a Gaussian and matrix B is initialized to zero so the initial forward pass equals the pretrained model.
claims.notes: reset_parameters zero-initialises B as stated but initialises A with nn.init.kaiming_uniform_, not a Gaussian. Corrected 2026-10-27: was VERIFIED with LoRALayer (which holds only r/alpha/dropout) as the relevant symbol.

claims.text: The merged weight matrix can be recomputed at inference by folding B A back into W_0 so no extra latency is incurred.
Only the low-rank matrices A and B receive gradient updates during training; the original weight matrix is frozen.
claims.notes: Linear.__init__ sets weight.requires_grad = False; mark_only_lora_as_trainable freezes every non-lora_ parameter. Corrected 2026-10-27: the relevant symbol was LoRALayer, which does neither.

claims.text: The library exposes a helper that marks only the LoRA parameters of a model as trainable and freezes all others.
claims.notes: Corrected 2026-10-27: the text said the helper replaces layers' forward methods, which the library does not do (layers are swapped for lora.Linear by hand).

claims.text: The example training script applies LoRA to GPT-2 attention layers and trains on the E2E dataset.
The GLUE benchmark evaluation fine-tunes RoBERTa with LoRA adapters on each task.
The lora_state_dict helper extracts only the trainable A and B matrices for checkpoint saving.
Rank r and scaling factor alpha are configurable hyperparameters of the LoRA layer.
